patch.value: A guarded restore of an item a storage override moved out of the tracker matches its revision entry only by the probe spelling, not the former embedded id

Found by CodeRabbit on PR 1658 (pm-thbdxu). When an item_store_write override redirects an item out of the tracker, the expected-revision scope advances to the empty tombstone. The write path now also carries the written embedded id as an advancement alias (as delete does), but a later guarded restore of the absent item resolves its target from history and matches scope entries by that probe spelling only. On a case-insensitive filesystem, a scope bound to the former embedded id under another spelling (PM-A vs pm-a) would not be judged by the restore. It is unreachable on case-sensitive filesystems, where the probe and embedded id of a bindable item are equal.

A guarded restore of an item that a storage override moved out of the tracker judges the scope entry bound to the item's former embedded id, whatever spelling located it, with a spec that simulates a case-variant probe; A peer write between the redirected write and the restore still refuses the restore with item_revision_conflict
Restore after a redirected write is judged against the entry bound to the former embedded id
Restore matches scope entries by the probe spelling only

message: File restore alias follow-up from CodeRabbit PR 1658
